To begin with, I've played this game partway through a half dozen times over the last ~20 years. None recently. Never beat it, either. I'm conversant in Japanese to the point where understanding the dialogue will probably be an adventure in itself. I have, incidentally, played FF6 in French and FF5 in Portuguese, being something of a faggot polyglot who feels better about wasting huge amounts of time if it's at least quasi-educational.

If you didn't know, text does matter in this game. It has this "aikotoba" dialogue system, "aikotoba" meaning something like "password" or "shibboleth", but definitely not "words of love" as you might literally translate it— it's written "合い言葉", not "愛言葉". The gist of the system is that when an NPC mentions a keyword, you can oboeru it and tazuneru other NPCs about it later. You can also "item" at the people you meet, which I'm sure will be real handy if we find a giant purple dildo somewhere to systematically present to every NPC in the game.

Another bit of fun I might add to the mix: Lua scripting. FCEUX allows the user to automate button presses programmatically. It's easy to exploit bugs in the much reviled combat system to gain absurd power with very little effort. Raising a character's weapon skill level, for example, only requires one to input a 'fight' command, pick a target, then cancel the next character's input, and the game increments the attacking character's attack level as if they'd actually executed the attack. IIRC, the skill counter is capped upon reaching the necessary skill points to level up a particular skill, which would mean you can get one weapon skill level per fight by running this:

-- FF2 weapon level bogotifier

-- skipframes is used to add delay between buttonpresses
-- to account for menu lag/animation.

function skipframes(framecount)
 for i = 0, framecount do
 emu.frameadvance()
 end
end

-- increment_skill sends the desired controller inputs

function increment_skill()
 -- select 'fight'
 joypad.set(1, {A=1})
 skipframes(20)
 -- pick an enemy
 joypad.set(1, {A=1})
 skipframes(40)
 -- cancel the next character
 joypad.set(1, {B=1})
 skipframes(40)
end

-- The above code only defines functions; the execution happens below.
-- It's a "forever loop" that reads player 2's controller state.
-- When the select button is pressed, the script begins the input macro at max emu speed.
-- Otherwise it runs the emulator as it normally runs.

-- The point, then, is to be in combat with the cursor on the character you want to level up
-- before pressing select.

while true do
 pad2 = joypad.read(2)
 if pad2['select'] then
 emu.speedmode("maximum")
 for i = 1, 100 do
 increment_skill()
 end
 emu.speedmode("normal")
 end
 emu.frameadvance()
end

You can automate battles, perhaps on condition that "enemy_lvl < player_lvl / 2" or some other situation where you want to omit boring, trivial battles from your gaming experience, like in Earthbound. The judicious application of a turing-complete programming language opens the door to all sorts of challenge runs without having to dirty your hands with 6502 assembly code.
